author: Luke Larson
title: Grant Wood's Corn Room Mural to reopen at Sioux City Art Center Saturday following restoration - NewsBreak
text:
By Luke Larson ,
1 hours ago
SIOUX CITY , Iowa ( KCAU ) — A century-old mural created by one of Iowa’s most famous artists is back in Sioux City.
The Siouxland and South Sioux City Chambers of Commerce held a ribbon-cutting ceremony on Wednesday to celebrate the reopening of Grant Wood’s Corn Room mural at the Sioux City Art Center.
The mural spent two years undergoing restoration in Minnesota.
Additionally, the “Pasture to Present” exhibit opens this week, featuring artwork that showcases the American Midwest.
Story continues below
Art Center staff say it’s a unique opportunity to experience the nearly 100-year-old mural.
“It’s really nice to look back. I mean, no one was around 100 years ago. It’s nice to imagine what it was like to see this when it was originally installed, and then to see it with these other paintings,” said Sioux City Art Center Curator Christopher Atkins.
Atkins said that the viewing experience is more similar to its original state now that the mural has been restored.
“Essentially, they make sure that they can preserve as much of what was there, and prevent any further damage from happening. What we want is this mural to look its best, and see it with other pieces that were made around the same time that Grant Wood was painting this,” said Atkins.
The public is invited to view the exhibit during a free reception on Saturday, June 13, from 5 p.m. to 7 p.m.
